robinhood.name: Robinhood
robinhood.key_insight: Robinhood is the most controversial case study in behavioral design because it reveals what happens when you apply consumer-app engagement techniques to financial instruments. The confetti animation on trades, the one-tap execution, the push notifications on price movements — these are standard mobile engagement patterns, except the 'engagement' involves real money and real financial risk. The SEC's 2021 investigation and subsequent $65M fine specifically cited Robinhood's gamification. Robinhood's defense — that simplicity democratizes access — is valid. The counterargument — that simplicity in high-stakes domains removes protective friction — is also valid. This tension makes Robinhood the defining case study for when behavioral design ethics actually matter.
robinhood.top_technique: Confetti and Celebration UI as Operant Conditioning

whatsapp.name: WhatsApp
whatsapp.key_insight: WhatsApp is the anti-TikTok: instead of sophisticated algorithmic manipulation, it uses radical simplicity and network effects as its behavioral architecture. The product doesn't need to hook you with variable rewards because your social obligations do the work. Blue ticks create response pressure, group chats create FOMO, and the social graph creates switching costs — all without a single gamification element. WhatsApp proves that the most powerful behavioral design can be invisible: no streaks, no likes, no algorithmic feed — just the weight of your social connections.
whatsapp.top_technique: Blue Ticks as Social Obligation Architecture
